claude.sample_unit: LLM responses to 42 diabetic retinopathy questions

links.outcome: Reading grade level of LLM responses to diabetic retinopathy questions versus recommended sixth-to-seventh grade level
links.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade levels ranged 12.6 (Bing Chat) to 16.0 (ChatGPT-3.5); all but 36 of 252 responses were above high school graduate reading level.
links.quote: Of the 252 LLM-generated responses, all but 36 were at a reading level above that of a high school graduate.

links.outcome: Readability of patient-directed LLM responses relative to NIH recommended reading level
links.effect: Responses were at college reading level (FK grade 12.6-16.0) versus NIH-recommended sixth/seventh grade; ChatGPT-3.5 Flesch Reading Ease 19.4.
links.quote: However, our findings reveal a significant discrepancy between this recommended standard and the actual reading level of LLM outputs.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM DR answers graded by three ophthalmologists
links.effect: 93.3% (235/252) good, 12 borderline, 5 poor; ChatGPT-4.0, ChatGPT-3.5 and QWEN 97.6% good; Bing Chat and Llama 2 85.7% good, Bing 9.5% poor.
links.quote: In terms of accuracy, 93.3% of the responses (235/252) to DR-related questions answered by LLMs received a ‘good’ grading, 12 responses received a ‘borderline’ grading and 5 responses received a ‘poor’ grading.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM responses across repeated queries
links.effect: Responses were collected only once per query; authors note repeated queries can produce different results, so the responses cannot be reliably regenerated verbatim.
links.quote: It should be noted that repeated queries to the same LLM, even in rapid succession, can produce different results.

links.outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy by domain (aetiology, treatment vs others)
links.effect: Excellent performance for established domains (symptoms, diagnosis, prevention, prognosis) but variable in cause and treatment domains, possibly outdated or textbook-only treatments.
links.quote: However, it is worth noting that the performance of the LLMs in the ‘cause’ and ‘treatment’ domains varied.

links.outcome: LLM ability to self-correct when prompted that answer seems wrong
links.effect: Mean accuracy score rose from 6.4±0.8 to 7.5±1.6; 70.6% (n=12) improved, 23.5% (n=4) decreased, 5.9% (n=1) unchanged.
links.quote: After self-corrections, the average accuracy score of the responses improved, rising from an initial value of 6.4±0.8 to 7.5±1.6 post-correction.

unlisted_practices: Self-correction prompting (asking the LLM to re-answer) to improve response accuracy
